answer:
Not accepted under the declared gates. Gate 1 and gate 3 pass; gate 2 fails by one finding: the adjudicator called 8 Terra findings invalid across 15 rounds, 0.53 per round against the declared ceiling of 0.5. One of the 8 reached a final list, within the declared limit of one. The holdout is ranked: the live Opus-against-Opus control differs by one unique valid cause.

What the arms did: Terra raised 108 Codex-side findings against Sol's 56 over the same 15 rounds, 56 valid majors against 23, and 7 valid causes Sol never raised against 4 the other way, at 53% of Sol's Codex tokens and 4.7 minutes per round against 6.2. Sol had no invalid finding among its 45 adjudicated; Terra had 8 among 84. Five of the 8 are majors, and every one of the five names a missing test or a test fixture (three "the browser test does not check X" findings on ttrpg-pr-152, "the journald step stops the install in the test container" and "no test covers a service failure and a prune failure together" on homelab-feat-8). The adjudicator's basis for every finding was a reproduced defect in the frozen code, and a missing test is not one. Synthesis removed three of the five majors and merged one; one minor reached a final list.

The declared rule stands and the production profile stays on Sol. The five majors are listed under the human pass: if the owner reads one of them as valid under this repository's own test rules, gate 2 passes at 7 in 15 and the three gates hold.
gates_prose: The margin of 3 on gate 1 came from the pilot's Sol-against-Sol spread (6 against 4 over nine rounds, scaled to fifteen). Gate 2's ceiling of 0.5 per round came from the pilot's 4 invalid Terra findings in 9 rounds. The Opus side, identical in both arms, ran at 1.4 invalid per round in both (21 and 20 in 15 rounds, 5 and 4 on final lists), so the ceiling the holdout declared for Terra is one the fixed Claude side does not meet; the rule was declared and is applied as declared.
cases: Five, one per corpus repository, none of the three pilot cases, the r249 labelled cases kept out: mms-pr-525 (my-mac-setup PR #525, 3 files), homelab-feat-8 (9 files, touches CLAUDE.md), ttrpg-pr-152 (6 files), platform-prd-3672 (10 files, touches a skill document), ux-chain-prd-3567 (7 files). Frozen detached checkouts at the SHAs in cases/.
budget: Rounds ran one at a time on 2026-10-29 from 20:06 to 22:52, case order mms, ux-chain, homelab, platform, ttrpg, baseline before Terra, repetition 1 to 3 in separate task directories with a fresh task identity per round. Thirty of thirty rounds completed, none degraded, actual model equal to requested in every manifest. Claude weekly quota 45% → 50% (51% after adjudication), Codex 5% → 8%; neither cap (60%) was reached and the five-hour window never waited.
limits:
• One adjudicator per case, OpenCode gpt-5.6-terra: it shares a vendor with the Terra arm. Its basis for every finding here was a reproduced defect; it did not use a prior human verdict or a recorded mutation.
  • The gate 2 verdict rests on how the adjudicator treats a missing test. All five invalid Terra majors are test-coverage or test-fixture findings. Sol raised none of that kind, so it had no exposure to the same standard.
  • No Sol-against-Sol pair in this design; the margin is the pilot's. Fifteen rounds per arm over five cases: in the baseline arm the same valid cause appeared in all three repetitions of its case for a minority of causes (the stability table), so a one-cause difference is inside the noise.
  • Terra wrote several finding titles in Russian on the two repositories whose agent documents are in Russian; synthesis kept them and the adjudicator read them. Not scored.
next:
1. The human pass on the five Terra majors and the one kept minor in the table above. One overturned major makes gate 2 pass and the holdout accept Terra; none overturned keeps Sol.
  2. If Terra is accepted: a separate PR that changes the Codex model in the managed profiles, with this record as its evidence. The Opus side's invalid rate, 1.4 per round on both arms, is the next thing worth a measurement of its own.
